docs/figures/kernel-compile-barrier/poin.contrast: passes: all text is near-black (#0b0b0b) or span grey (#595959) on white, the control bar is mid grey (#999999) against white, and the stubbed bars are blue (#3366cc), each well separated from the ground it sits on
docs/figures/kernel-compile-barrier/poin.data_ink: passes: one flat bar per block and per arm carries the ink, and the only other marks are two thin grey span arrows and their labels; no gradient, marker cloud or second geometry competes with the bars
docs/figures/kernel-compile-barrier/poin.decoration: passes: white ground throughout, no gridline in either panel (a column scan of both plot interiors found no uniform full-height line), no background band or fill, and only the left and bottom spines carry a scale
docs/figures/kernel-compile-barrier/poin.label_collision: passes: no label is clipped, and the pixel scan found no collision — the corner-height span arrow stands at x=1062 with the '104.5' label at x=1105-1151, 43 px clear of the shaft, and the derivative span arrow at x=1193 is 47 px from the '34.1' label; the rotated span labels sit in the inter-bar gaps, clear of both bars and arrows
docs/figures/kernel-compile-barrier/poin.legibility: readable at a glance: the left panel ranks five source blocks by the share of the 6,088,067-byte lowered graph their stub removes, with the erased block stated in words on its own row; the right panel shows three compiled arms in cold H200 seconds, each with a dark value label above its bar, and the two grey spans are labelled in the gaps beside the bars
docs/figures/kernel-compile-barrier/poin.table_form: passes: both panels compare magnitudes, where the comparison itself is a length; a table would not show relative size, and the erased block states its categorical outcome in the word 'erased' rather than pretending to a bar length

findings.summary: The left panel's four shares sum to 215.2 per cent, because the stubs are nested: the value-path stub removes the derivative tower, the corner-height Hessian and the elliptic terms with it. A reader who adds the bars, which the axis invites by expressing every one of them as a percentage of the same 6,088,067 bytes, gets more than the whole and has no cue on the panel that the rows are overlapping measurements rather than a partition. The new work in this commit has made the legend honest about state; the same panel still reads as a breakdown.

The legend's dotted swatch for the erased state denotes a mark that appears nowhere in the picture. The erased row's bar is drawn with zero length and a solid edge at x=0, where the y-axis spine covers it, so no dotted element is rendered on either panel while the legend shows a dotted one; a reader scanning for the mark the legend describes finds nothing. The legend's own words ('zero-length bar, marked in text, no share') carry the meaning, which is why this does not hold the node.
